headlines.title: Man repairs 2 wrecked Teslas, they pass inspection, but the carmaker cuts fast charging anyway — now he owes $15K
headlines.summary: Vehicles that Tesla has not confirmed comply with its safety standards could damage a Supercharger or might not be safe to drive, the company says.

headlines.title: Tesla Bears Are Falling Off But Not Because Tesla’s Improving
headlines.summary: Tesla short sellers are retreating, but the reason has nothing to do with the company fixing its collapsing margins or surging profits. A single rumor reshuffled the entire bearish case overnight, and now the stock sits exactly at Wall Street's consensus target with nowhere obvious to go.

headlines.title: Tesla's Free Cash Flow Just Turned Positive. Here's Why That's Only Half the Story.
headlines.summary: The reason is because the company made about $3 billion less in capital expenditure than expected, not that its business improved.

headlines.title: Tesla Closed Up 4% at $407. Here’s What a SpaceX Merger Could Mean for Your Shares.
headlines.summary: A possible Tesla and SpaceX combination has Elon Musk calling it a good idea, Wall Street assigning a 52% probability, and at least one prominent critic labeling it a rescue operation in disguise. Here is what each possible outcome does to your shares.

headlines.title: Tesla (TSLA) Could Be 223% Overvalued After Flat Revenue And Lower Profit
headlines.summary: Tesla (TSLA) has just reported third quarter 2026 earnings that showed revenue broadly flat at US$28.0b while net income declined to US$787 million, sharpening investor focus on profitability and capital allocation. Tesla’s recent earnings setback has played out against a sharp swing in sentiment, with the share price up 36.6% over 90 days and 9.5% over the past month, yet still down 7.0% year to date and delivering an 11.5% decline in 1-year total shareholder return.

description: Tesla, Inc. designs, develops, manufactures, leases, and sells electric vehicles, and energy generation and storage systems in the United States, China, and internationally. The company operates in two segments, Automotive; and Energy Generation and Storage. The company offers electric vehicles, as well as sells automotive regulatory credits; and non-warranty maintenance services and collision, automotive insurance services, as well as part sales and retail merchandise sale. It also provides sedans and sport utility vehicles through direct and used vehicle sales, a network of Tesla Superchargers, and in-app upgrades; purchase financing and leasing services; services for electric vehicles through its company-owned service locations and Tesla mobile service technicians; and vehicle limited warranties and extended service plans. In addition, the company engages in the design, manufacture, installation, sale, and leasing of solar energy generation and energy storage products, and related services to residential, commercial, and industrial customers and utilities through its website, stores, and galleries, as well as through a network of channel partners. Further, it provides services and repairs to its energy product customers, including under warranty and extended service plans; and various financing options to its residential customers; lithium-ion battery energy storage products, such as Powerwall and Megapack; energy generation products, including solar panels and solar roof; self-driving development and artificial intelligence software, vehicle control and infotainment software, and battery and powertrain. The company was formerly known as Tesla Motors, Inc. and changed its name to Tesla, Inc. in February 2017. Tesla, Inc. was incorporated in 2003 and is headquartered in Austin, Texas.
